newsitem.title: USA: Clinton meets Rep. Richardson, who could get top job.
newsitem.headline: Clinton meets Rep. Richardson, who could get top job.

text.p: President Bill Clinton met privately at the White House late on Tuesday with Representative Bill Richardson as senior officials said he was under consideration for a top administration post.

"I would not read too much into this," said Deputy White House Press Secretary Mary Ellen Glynn as she confirmed that the New Mexico Democrat met with Clinton after spending several hours talking with other officials at the White House.

Administration officials said Richardson had been under consideration for several possible posts, including U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, head of the Commerce Department or other Cabinet positions.
Officials said Clinton was conducting what one called "a series of job interviews," but stressed that it was unlikely that any major announcements were imminent.
Richardson has earned a reputation for his successful trouble-shooting trips abroad. As an administration emissary, he has negotiated with leaders in Burma, Haiti, North Korea and Iraq.

In November he made a trip to North Korea that won the release of a young American detained for three months on espionage charges. He travelled this month to a remote area of Sudan to help win the release of three Red Cross workers held hostage by a rebel leader.
